cues.text: Section four is about ISO standards and how to select a framework.
Let us begin with ISO/IEC 38500.
This standard provides principles for governing bodies to evaluate, direct and monitor the use of IT.
The familiar course-book principles are responsibility, strategy, acquisition, performance, conformance and human behaviour.
Notice that this is executive-oriented guidance.
It is not a certifiable information security management system, so an organisation cannot be certified against it in that sense.
Next, ISO/IEC 27001.
This standard specifies requirements for an information security management system, usually shortened to ISMS.
An ISMS is a managed system made up of policies, responsibilities, risk assessment, controls, monitoring and improvement.
Organisations can seek certification against its requirements.
Be careful to separate it from ISO/IEC 27002, which provides control guidance, not the same certification requirements.
So 27001 gives the requirements you can be certified against, while 27002 offers guidance on controls.
Then there is ISO/IEC 20000-1, which specifies certifiable service management system requirements.
Now let us read the table that helps with framework selection.
It has two columns: the need, and the best fit.
I will go row by row.
First row: when the need is enterprise IT governance and control objectives, the best fit is COBIT.
Second row: when the need is executive oversight and responsible use of IT, the best fit is ISO/IEC 38500.
Third row: when the need is reliable IT service delivery and improvement, the best fit is ITIL.
Fourth row: when the need is certifiable information security management, the best fit is ISO/IEC 27001.
Fifth and last row: when the need is certifiable service management, the best fit is ISO/IEC 20000-1.
Notice how the table separates the needs.
Two of the rows stress certifiability, namely 27001 for information security and 20000-1 for service management, while the others address governance, oversight and service delivery practice.
Finally, these frameworks and standards are complementary, not competing choices.
For example, a hospital may use COBIT to establish accountability, ISO 27001 to manage information security, and ITIL to run its support desk.
One organisation can therefore draw on several of them, each for the job it fits best.
And remember an important qualification: certification does not guarantee that no breach or outage will occur.
